name: Graviola
workload: TLS certificate/handshake crypto ops (RSA-PSS, ECDSA P-256/P-384, Ed25519 signing across secp256r1/secp384r1/x25519 key exchange) benchmarked via hyperfine, comparing aws-lc-rs, Graviola, ring and OpenSSL
claimed_speedup: "OpenSSL is the slower library" and "Graviola is a promising new cryptography library" (per-op box-plot timings on a 0-10ms axis; exact values are only in embedded SVG charts, not present as page text)
hardware: AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12-Core, 32GB DDR4, Linux Fedora kernel 7.0.11-200.fc44.x86_64
tradeoffs: Rust only; requires aarch64 with NEON+PMULL or x86_64 with AVX2/ADX/BMI2/PCLMULQDQ (excludes older CPUs like Raspberry Pi 4); very new/unaudited; RSA key generation is not side-channel-safe; built primarily as a rustls CryptoProvider rather than a standalone TLS stack
caveats: Independent third-party benchmark (author of the wtx project) shows OpenSSL as the slowest of 4 libraries and calls Graviola promising, but states no compiler version/flags, and its numeric results live only inside embedded SVG box-plot images rather than page text/tables. Graviola's own first-party benchmark page (jbp.io/graviola/, by the same author as Graviola/rustls) additionally shows Graviola winning several ops (ECDSA-P256 signing, X25519, ML-KEM-768) against ring/aws-lc-rs/rustcrypto/dalek on Apple M2 and AMD Ryzen 9 7940HS, but that comparison set does not include OpenSSL/BoringSSL/rustls directly, so it was not used as the primary citation.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): HN Algolia query "TLS handshake performance" -> c410-f3r blog post; cross-checked via gh search repos "graviola" and gh api repos/ctz/graviola

name: Fizz
workload: Facebook load-balancer production traffic comparing Fizz's AsyncFizzServer/Client TLS 1.3 implementation against folly's prior AsyncSSLSocket-based TLS stack
claimed_speedup: "we found in our load balancer benchmarks that Fizz has 10% higher throughput than our prior SSL library which uses folly's AsyncSSLSocket"; also states Fizz uses less memory per connection
stars_or_usage: 1.2k stars; used in production at Facebook/Meta load balancers
tradeoffs: Depends on folly (IOBuf, AsyncTransportWrapper), a large dependency graph; C++14 only; scatter/gather in-place encryption trades API simplicity for the throughput/memory win
caveats: First-party (Meta) README claim with no published benchmark methodology, hardware, or reproducible artifact; the '10%' number is stated but not backed by linked data. 'Prior SSL library' is folly's AsyncSSLSocket, which wraps OpenSSL in Meta's public folly build -- the closest nameable baseline, but the exact library/version at benchmark time is not specified.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): HN Algolia query "Fizz TLS Facebook" -> facebookincubator/fizz repo; README Performance section read via gh api repos/facebookincubator/fizz/readme

name: AWS-LC
workload: HAProxy 3.1-dev server-side full TLS handshake and TLS-resumption connections/sec benchmark on a 64-core AWS Graviton4 instance
claimed_speedup: AWS-LC (post-v1.32.0, recompiled with C11) sustains "above 63000 connections per second" for full handshakes vs ~48,000/s for OpenSSL 1.1.1 and ~42,500/s for OpenSSL 3.1-3.4-dev; in TLS resumption AWS-LC 1.29.0 reaches ~183,000 conn/s, "about 20% higher than WolfSSL and 50% higher than OpenSSL 1.1.1w", and vastly ahead of OpenSSL 3.0.x (~1,500-8,000 conn/s)
compiler_and_flags: AWS-LC recompiled with C11 (vs its C99 default, which caused suboptimal reference counting); HAProxy 3.1-dev1-ad946a-33 (2024/06/26); tested against OpenSSL 1.1.1, 3.0.2, 3.0.14, 3.1-3.4-dev
hardware: AWS r8g.16xlarge, 64x AWS Graviton4 (ARM Neoverse V2) cores
stars_or_usage: 835 stars; AWS's default crypto/TLS backend across many AWS services
tradeoffs: Result is highly compiler-flag sensitive (C99 vs C11 materially changes AWS-LC's reference-counting performance); AWS-LC and OpenSSL versions compared were not all captured at the same point in time
caveats: AWS-LC is already catalogued (KNOWN_LIST: https://github.com/aws/aws-lc); reported here ONLY as is_evidence_for_known=true because this independent, version- and hardware-pinned HAProxy benchmark is Tier A evidence of it beating OpenSSL directly. Benchmark tool (h1load, https://github.com/wtarreau/h1load) is public but the full test harness/scripts are not linked in the post.
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): HN Algolia query "state of SSL stacks" -> HAProxy blog "The State of SSL Stacks"

name: wolfSSL
workload: Same HAProxy 3.1-dev server-side TLS handshake and TLS-resumption connections/sec benchmark on the 64-core AWS Graviton4 instance
claimed_speedup: wolfSSL 5.7.0 sustains ~150,000 conn/s in TLS resumption vs OpenSSL 1.1.1w's ~124,000 conn/s (with HAProxy's optimized locks) -- roughly 20% higher -- and is vastly ahead of OpenSSL 3.0.x (~1,500-8,000 conn/s, described as "1/100 of WolfSSL's performance"); full-handshake throughput (~48,000/s) roughly matches OpenSSL 1.1.1 and beats OpenSSL 3.1-3.4-dev (~42,500/s)
hardware: AWS r8g.16xlarge, 64x AWS Graviton4 (ARM Neoverse V2) cores
tradeoffs: GPL-3.0 (dual-licensed; commercial license required for closed-source distribution); trailed AWS-LC in the same benchmark (~48k vs ~63k handshakes/s)
caveats: wolfSSL is already catalogued (KNOWN_LIST: https://github.com/wolfssl/wolfssl); reported here ONLY as is_evidence_for_known=true, since this independent HAProxy Tier A benchmark separately shows it beating OpenSSL directly. (A separate wolfSSL-vs-mbedTLS first-party benchmark from wolfssl.com was found and excluded: it is Tier C, first-party, and mbedTLS is not one of OpenSSL/BoringSSL/rustls.)
found_via: Independent benchmark suites and blogs (shootouts; harvest their winners): HN Algolia query "state of SSL stacks" -> HAProxy blog "The State of SSL Stacks"
